summary: Plan v12, Phases 0-1 (verification spike; sat_timp field) were already [COMPLETED] before this dispatch. blockers.description: Phase 3's mandated timeboxed alternative check found that the plan's stated world-bound proof strategy -- an injective map from world-creation events into distinct static .imp-node positions of phi0 (backed by intSubfmls_impCount_le) -- is false, verified by a concrete, reproducible counterexample computed directly against the real intuitionisticTableau/intApplyRuleFull functions (not a hand-proof stall). For phi0 = ((p->q)->r /\ (s->t)) -> ((u1->v1) \/ (u2->v2) \/ (u3->v3)) (complexity 10), the single static position 'p->q' fires the world-creating rule at 8 distinct labels, not 1, because the T-signed antecedent-of-antecedent gets copied (via propagatePersistence and applyAllTImpRules's broader accessible-world copy channel) into every sibling world created from its source, and each copy independently BETA-resolves and re-fires world-creation. Whether the target numeric bound (nextWorld <= phi0.complexity + 1) itself holds is unresolved either way -- only the specific proof route is refuted. Two follow-on stress tests intended to compound the effect timed out in the #eval sandbox before returning a conclusive result. See handoffs/12_world-bound-decision.md for full derivation, evidence, and three candidate re-plan directions (amortized/multiset argument, potential-function argument tied to the existing intExpMeasure machinery, or independent reverification of the bound via a faster instrumented harness).

decisions_made: Executed Phase 2's block relocation via a verified pure-Python line-slice splice rather than manual Edit tool operations, given the plan's own guidance to avoid whole-file reads and manual edits at this scale; verified purity via an exact sorted-multiset-of-lines identity check between pre- and post-move content.

dead_ends: The injection 'world-creation event -> distinct .imp-node position of phi0' (as literally stated in three pre-existing in-file docstrings and the plan's Phase 3/4 tasks) is refuted by direct counterexample -- do not attempt to formalize it as stated in a future dispatch.

Do not trust the in-file docstring's premise 'F-signed formulas never propagate via persistence' as sufficient justification for injectivity -- it is true but irrelevant: the T-signed antecedent-of-antecedent propagates, and each copy's own resolution mints a fresh F-signed instance independently.

Attempting to stress-test the numeric bound itself via nested implication chains (to amplify the counterexample and determine whether the bound is outright false, not just the proof route) hit #eval sandbox timeouts for chain depth >= 2; this needs a faster computational harness (native-compiled test or hand-instrumented tracing) before it can be resolved, not a bigger #eval budget in the same style.
